summary: Pema Wangchok Gyelpo studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shenphen Nangwa and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Linguist and Tibetologist Pema Wangdi earned degrees from the University of Delhi, RIM, and James Cook University (PhD 2021). His career includes posts at the UN Bhutanese Mission, Dzongkha Development Commission, and an adjunct fellowship at Central Queensland University (2023).
Peng Zhou works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Bachelor of Philosophy from Hunan Normal University (2013–2017) and a Master of Philosophy from Shaanxi Normal University (2017–2020).

Penghao Sun is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. Supervised by Leonard van der Kuijp, he also studied under Mark Elliott, Charles Hallisey, Peter K. Bol, Jay Jasanoff, James Robson, Ryuichi Abe, Jie Li, Weirong Shen, Qingying Chen, and Borjigidai Oyunbilig.
Penor 02 studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang. He also engaged in mutual study and teaching relationships with Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. Educated at Palyul Monastery under Thubten Chökyi Dawa, Karma Tekchok Nyingpo, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Jampel Gyepai Dorje, he founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1978 and taught numerous disciples.

Pent Nurmekund (1906–1996) was an Estonian linguist and Indologist. Educated at Tartu, Copenhagen, Gothenburg, and Paris under scholars including Friedrich Ernst Kieckers and Louis Trolle Hjelmslev, he held Humboldt scholarships in Germany and taught at the University of Tartu (1955–1986).

Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) was a Finnish scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki and Uppsala University, and served as a docent at the University of Helsinki from 1949 to 1980.

Per Kjeld Sørensen (b. 1950) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Copenhagen. He lectured at Copenhagen, served as professor at the University of Leipzig (1994–2017), and held visiting or fellow roles at Bonn and UC Berkeley.

Per Kværne (b. 1945) is a Norwegian scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Oslo. He held posts at the University of Bergen, University of Oslo, and the International Association for Tibetan Studies.
Per Persson (1857–1929) was a Swedish linguist. He studied at Uppsala University, where he later served as Professor of Latin Language and Literature beginning in 1895.

Per Vilhelm Hilding Juliusson (1916–1977) was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Uppsala University and Stockholm University, completing his Ph.D. under Åke Hultkrantz by 1974.

Percy Brown (1872–1955) worked in Indology and art history/archaeology. Educated at the Royal College of Art, he was Principal of the National College of Arts, Lahore, Principal of Calcutta's Government College of Art, and Secretary and Curator at Victoria Memorial (1927–1947).

Peri Bhaskararao (1947–2021) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Phonetics and Phonology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1978–1998) and later held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1998–2013).
Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) was an Indologist and linguist. He completed doctoral studies under Wilhelm Rau and served as a Lektor at the University of Marburg from 1964 to 1991.

Pero Slijepčević (1888–1964) was an Indologist and Germanist. After studying at the universities of Geneva and Fribourg (Ph.D. 1920), he served as Professor of Germanistics at the University of Sarajevo and the University of Belgrade (~1928–1941).

Perry Link (b. 1944) is an American Sinologist who studied at Harvard University. He held academic posts at Princeton University, the University of California, Los Angeles, and the University of California, Riverside.

Perry Schmidt-Leukel (b. 1954) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who completed his studies and habilitation at the University of Munich. He served as professor at the University of Glasgow (2000–2009) and University of Münster (2009–2023).
Pertti Valtonen (1933–1999) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Helsinki, earning his M.A. in 1964 and studying under Pentti Aalto through 1968.
Petar Budmani (1835–1914) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna in 1853 and later served as a professor at the Dubrovnik Gymnasium from 1868 to 1882.
